title: DOW-UAP-D19, Mission Report, Syria, February 21, 2023
what_is_it: U.S. military Mission Report (MISREP) documenting a Defensive Counter-Air (DCA) sortie by F-15E aircraft over Syria in support of Operation Inherent Resolve, during which the crew observed possible UAPs and a possible balloon.
interpretation_warnings: Heavy redactions throughout: coordinates, callsigns, specific locations, and personal identifying information are redacted under FOIA exemptions (b)(3), (b)(6), and classification sections 1.4a and 1.4g

UAP descriptions are the crew's subjective characterization — the report itself notes 'such characterizations should not be interpreted as a conclusive indication of the presence or absence of any intrinsic object features or performance characteristics'
The objects were described as 'possible' UAP and 'possible' balloon — these are not confirmed identifications
The UAPs produced no radar returns on the APG-82, which could indicate small size, low radar cross-section, or sensor limitations — but could also reflect environmental conditions or other factors
The 3 UAP and 1 balloon are logged as separate AIRSIGHT events approximately 70 minutes apart, at different altitudes (FL240 vs FL210)
Weapon System Video (WSV) was recorded for both sightings but is not included in this document release
Single-source report from one aircrew; no corroborating sensor data or independent observer reports are included
OCR artifacts throughout the document make some text ambiguous; redacted classification markings appear garbled
The radar jamming event occurred minutes before the first UAP sighting — temporal proximity may or may not be relevant

public_headline: F-15E Crew Reports Unidentified Objects Over Syria During 2023 Mission
public_tldr: A formerly secret U.S. military mission report describes an F-15E fighter crew observing three possible unidentified aerial phenomena and one possible balloon over eastern Syria on February 21, 2023. The objects produced no radar returns but were visible on infrared sensors, and the crew had experienced radar jamming minutes before the first sighting.
public_narrative:
This document is a U.S. Department of War mission report from the 389th Expeditionary Fighter Squadron, originally classified SECRET and released on 8 October 2025 by Major General Richard A. Harrison, USCENTCOM Chief of Staff. It records a Defensive Counter-Air sortie — an air-defense patrol — flown by two F-15E Strike Eagles (tail numbers 169 and 188) out of Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan on the night of February 20–21, 2023, in support of Operation Inherent Resolve over Syria.

During the nearly five-hour mission, the crew reported two separate sighting events near the town of Shaddadi. At approximately 0025Z, they observed three possible unidentified aerial phenomena at Flight Level 240 (roughly 24,000 feet). The objects appeared as two white shapes that registered on infrared sensors but produced no returns on the aircraft's APG-82 radar. About 70 minutes later, at 0135Z, the crew observed a single possible balloon at Flight Level 210 (roughly 21,000 feet) in the same area. Weapon System Video was recorded for both events but is not included in this release. No health effects were reported by the aircrew.

Minutes before the first sighting, the crew experienced three minutes of radar jamming on the 8.8–9.9 GHz frequency band, which partially degraded their APG-82 radar. The report's working theory attributes this to a Turkish X-band jammer operating near the Syria–Turkey border, not to the observed objects.

The document is heavily redacted. Coordinates, callsigns, crew names, and specific locations are blacked out under Freedom of Information Act exemptions. The report does not offer a final determination on what the objects were — the crew's descriptions are explicitly noted as preliminary, using the word "possible" for both the UAP and the balloon.
public_caveats: This is a single-source report from one aircrew. No corroborating sensor data or independent observer accounts are included in the release.

The crew described the objects as "possible" UAP and a "possible" balloon — these are not confirmed identifications, and the report itself cautions against treating crew characterisations as conclusive.
Heavy redactions remove coordinates, callsigns, and personal details, making independent verification of specifics difficult.
Weapon System Video was recorded for both sightings but has not been released with this document.

The radar jamming event occurred minutes before the first UAP sighting. The report attributes the jamming to a Turkish source, not to the objects, but the temporal proximity is noted without explanation.
